items.title: Hormuz hits us on both sides: ore can't come in, pellets and steel can't go out
items.facts: Traffic is at 5% of normal and war-risk insurance at about 32 times usual. Most companies face this on one side; we face it on both, so the risk doubles.
items.decision: Build ore stock now and set up a route that avoids the strait (ports outside it, the GCC railway) before competitors book the capacity.

items.title: Cheap ore and scarce pellets: the best pellet margin in two years, but it won't last
items.facts: Iron ore is near a 2-year low (about $91) while Ferrexpo's halt tightens pellet supply in Europe. The window closes as soon as Ukraine gets its power back.
items.decision: Lock in ore at today's prices and sell pellets forward to Ferrexpo's European customers this quarter.

items.title: Gas, not ore, now limits DRI-based steel in the Middle East and North Africa
items.facts: Egypt cut its mills' gas by 30% and Italian mills shut on energy costs. In this market, whoever has secure gas wins market share.
items.decision: Treat our gas contract as a strategic asset, and fill Egypt's shortfall with billets, sections or HBI.

items.title: The Saudi investigation could give GCC section mills their home market back
items.facts: Duties on Chinese and Turkish sections would reshape the biggest market around us. The companies that supply data to the investigation help decide where the duties land.
items.decision: File data in support now and plan the sales capacity to take the share that frees up.

items.title: Europe is putting up walls, so diverted steel will head for the GCC
items.facts: Out-of-quota EU tariffs of 50% (still to confirm) push Chinese, Indian and Turkish steel to look for other buyers. Our region is the obvious next market for that steel.
items.decision: Prepare for lower import prices into the GCC, and use this to argue for stronger Gulf trade defence.

items.title: Europe's green-steel delay gives us time, not a cancelled market
items.facts: thyssenkrupp has pushed its DRI plant to 2029 and POSCO's new furnace runs at 10% of capacity. European buyers are unsure right now, which is when long-term contracts are cheapest to win.
items.decision: Sign DR-grade pellet supply deals now, backed by product carbon footprints; our gas-DRI route beats blast furnaces under CBAM.

items.title: Simandou shifts profit from mining the ore to processing it
items.facts: More high-grade ore lowers the price floor for iron ore from 2027. Good pellet feed gets cheaper, so value moves to plants that turn ore into pellets.
items.decision: Renegotiate long-term ore contracts down, and test Simandou ore in our pellet plants.
